• Mahayana Buddhism:
 
 
• After the death of Buddha, a group evolved who believed that compassion for all humanity was an important part of the path, and that teaching is fully available to all.
 
• Those who followed the newly expanded ideals called themselves Mahayana meaning the big raft.
 
• In Mahayana Buddhism, all practicing Buddhists are apprentice Bodhisattvas.
 
• In Mahayana countries, images of the Buddha are set up in the temples and homes as an object of worship.
 
 
 
• Hinayana Buddhism:
 
 
• From about 100 years after the death of the Buddha, there had been a movement towards embracing the style of Buddhism.
 
• The early monks concentrated on personal enlightenment, seeking spiritual answers for themselves, and teaching others the way of enlightenment.
 
• But the information was severely limited to the lay community as it was assumed only minks could achieve Buddhahood.
 
• This section came to be known as Hinayana or also known as Theravada.
 
• Theravada means the way of elders.
 
 
 
• Milindapanha:
 
 
• The Milindapanha, or "Milinda's Questions," is an important early Buddhist text that usually is not included in the Pali Canon.
 
• Even so, the Milindapanha is cherished because it addresses many of Buddhism's most difficult doctrines with wit and clarity. 
 
• The Milindapanha presents a dialogue between King Menander I (Milinda in Pali) and an enlightened Buddhist monk named Nagasena.
 
• Menander- I was an Indo-Greek king thought to have ruled from about 160 to 130 BCE.
 
• He was a king of Bactria, an ancient kingdom that took in what is now Turkmenistan, Afghanistan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan, plus a small part of Pakistan.

questions.question: Which among the following period of the stone age **first** witnessed the domestication of animals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Mesolithic Age__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mesolithic Age falls roughly from **9000 B.C. to 4000 B.C**.
 
• It was the transitional phase between the Paleolithic Age and Neolithic Age.
 
• Although Mesolithic men were still dependent largely on hunting, now they used began **taming the animals** like dog, sheep, goat, cow-ox, buffalo, wild horse, etc.
 
• The earliest evidence of the taming of animals was found from **Adamgarh of Madhya Pradesh** and **Baghore of Rajasthan**. They are Mesolithic sites. **Hence, Option 4 is correct**.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Paleolithic: 

 
 
• It is the earliest Stone age period dating 2.6 million years ago.
 
• The age is distinguished by most primitive stone tools. Humans during the era grouped together in small “bands” and were involved in gathering plants, fishing, and hunting.
 
• The paleolithic period is the longest in human history.
 
• The age can be divided into lower Paleolithic, Middle Paleolithic, and Upper Paleolithic. 
 
• During the end of the age, people developed spiritual and religious beliefs as depicted in some of the excavations.
 
 
 
• Mesolithic: It is the second period of the stone age between Paleolithic and Neolithic. The start and end of the age vary by geographical region. It is a transition period from hunting and gathering as in Paleolithic to domestication as in Neolithic. The tools used were the mode V chipped stone tools (microliths).
 
• Neolithic: It is the 3rd period of the stone age and is often referred to as the “New stone age”. Its time period is considered to be around 10,200 BC to 4,500BC, which ended with the beginning of the “Bronze Age”.
 
• **Microlith**: It is a small tool made up of flint or chert, used to form the points of hunting weapons.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers flowed through Magadha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganga and Son.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Magadha became the most important Mahajana Pada in about two hundred years.
 
• The Ganga and Son Rivers flowed through Magadha.
 
• Magadha empire was established on the bank of the river Ganges and was bounded by the river Son on the west.
 
• Magadha was an ancient Indian kingdom in Bihar.
 
• The First capital of Magadha was Rajagriha.
 
• The first ruling dynasty of Magadha was the Haryak dynasty.
 
• Bimbasar ruled Magadha Empire for almost 52 years.
 
• Magadha finds mention in the Atharva Veda which conveys that Magadha was semi-Brahmanical habitation. 
 
• Later, Magadha became a center of Jainism and the first Buddhist Council was held in Rajagriha.

questions.question:
Arrange the following Chola rulers of the Sangam age in the chronological order: 

(i) Karikala 

(ii) Senganan

(iii) Elara

(iv) Iianjetcenni 

Select the answer from the codes below:
questions.solution:
The correct chronological code is __**​(iii) Elara (ii) Senganan (iv) Ilanjetcenni (i) Karikala**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**​Elara: **

 
• Elara is not traditionally listed among the early Cholas from the Sangam age due to a mix-up with historical figures.
 
• The Elara most commonly known in historical texts is Elara, a king of Sri Lanka who ruled over the Sinhalese kingdom of Anuradhapura.
 
• He is notable in Indian history for his just rule and is often not directly associated with the Chola dynasty of the Sangam age.
 
• However, the inclusion here may point to confusion or less commonly discussed aspects of early South Indian and Sri Lankan history.
 
• It's worth noting that ancient and medieval histories often blend, and records from those times might not always follow a clear lineage or detailed chronology.

**Senganan:**

 
• Senganan, also referred to as Senganan, was an early Chola king. However, very specific details about his reign or chronological placement are hard to find in historical texts. The Sangam literature, ancient Tamil literature, provides fragmented information about the early Chola rulers, making the precise chronology difficult.

**Ilanjetcenni: **

 
• Ilanjetcenni, also known as Ilanjetchenni, is mentioned in the Sangam literature as a valiant Chola king who fought several battles.
 
• His precise period is also challenging to determine, but he is celebrated for his military exploits and governance.
 
• These accounts highlight the valor and the expansionist activities of the early Cholas.

**Karikala: **

 
• Karikala Chola is one of the most renowned among early Chola kings and has a more detailed legend associated with him.
 
• He is acknowledged for consolidating the Chola kingdom after a period of strife and for significant infrastructure projects, the most famous being the construction of the Kallanai (Grand Anicut), an ancient dam across the Kaveri River in Tamil Nadu.
 
• He is traditionally placed in the early centuries CE, making him one of the latter rulers of this list in the chronological sense.
